hardRequirements: Applicant must be a current Colorado electric residential customer of Black Hills Energy.
For the 2026 residential rebate form, purchases and installations must be completed between January 1, 2026 and December 31, 2026, and applications for 2026 work must be received by January 31, 2027.
Customer must purchase and install the new equipment before submitting the rebate application.
Equipment and envelope measures must be installed in conditioned living spaces; garages and shops are not eligible.
Insulation, air sealing, and duct sealing require a home with a central cooling system.
Air sealing requires blower-door testing and duct sealing requires duct-blaster testing when applicable.
Central air conditioners and heat pumps require AHRI specification sheets and matched-system eligibility where applicable.

Applications must include receipts or itemized invoices with installation/service address, equipment details, manufacturer/model/serial numbers, installation date, costs, and contractor information where applicable.
Funding is limited; applications are processed first-come, first-served; installations may be inspected; used, reconditioned, or resale equipment is not eligible.
blockers: High-efficiency furnace retrofit is a false match for this electric residential record. The current electric rebate application supports furnace blower motor ECMs, not general furnace replacement; furnace rebates are on the separate Colorado gas residential program.

Generic commercial energy-management-system matching is not supported by this residential electric record. The supported current measure is residential home energy management, specifically smart power strips, and related residential controls.

Duct sealing is supported; a separate duct-insulation rebate was not found in the current electric residential application. The combined category is retained only because the taxonomy label includes duct sealing.
High-efficiency refrigeration is limited to residential refrigerator measures; do not map this record to commercial refrigeration, walk-in coolers/freezers, or refrigeration controls.

The official page includes EV charger rebate programs, but those appear as a separate Ready EV program on the same page and should be modeled as separate EV opportunities rather than folded into this DSIRE energy-efficiency record.
Residential Demand Response and Residential Online Marketplace programs are discontinued as of December 31, 2025 and should not be matched as current active rebates.
repairs.evidenceText: Black Hills Energy's current Colorado electric residential rebate page lists a residential rebate program with products including heat pumps, air conditioners, evaporative coolers, smart thermostats, water heaters, furnace blower motors, home appliances, and insulation and sealing; it also lists a home energy assessment kit with LED bulbs, faucet aerators, showerheads, and door weatherstripping. The same page says Residential Demand Response and Residential Online Marketplace are discontinued as of Dec. 31, 2025. The 2026 Colorado electric residential application lists central and room air conditioners, air-source, ductless mini-split, cold-climate, and geothermal heat pumps, smart thermostats, ENERGY STAR heat-pump water heaters, furnace blower ECMs, insulation, air sealing, duct sealing, smart power strips, air purifiers, dehumidifiers, ceiling fans, clothes washers, refrigerators, and radon fans. The application terms require current Colorado electric residential customer status, 2026 purchase/installation timing, application submission by Jan. 31, 2027, conditioned living-space installation, complete documentation, limited funding, and possible inspections. The beneficial-electrification application separately supports residential conversion from natural gas space or water heating to efficient electric equipment, including air-source heat pumps, geothermal heat pumps, ductless mini-splits, heat-pump water heaters, air sealing, insulation, duct sealing, panel upgrades, and heat-pump clothes dryers, with income-qualified provisions.
